claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC material with a dendritic microstructure.
The untreated TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The untreated TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K and 30% compressive strain.
Controlled oxygen addition during processing will promote in situ oxide-dispersoid formation in TiVNbTa.
The oxygen addition will produce uniformly distributed, nanometric oxide dispersoids within the BCC matrix.
The resulting oxide dispersoids will remain stable at approximately 1273 K.
The oxide dispersoids will impede dislocation motion at high temperature.
The oxide dispersoids will reduce grain-boundary sliding at high temperature.
Impeded dislocation motion and reduced grain-boundary sliding will retard high-temperature softening.
Oxygen-modified TiVNbTa will have a yield strength above approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Oxygen-modified TiVNbTa will have a compressive strength above approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K and 30% strain.
Testing at approximately 1273 K and up to 30% compressive strain is representative of service as a heat-transfer layer between tungsten and CuCrZr.
The proposed oxide-dispersion-strengthening mechanism is well supported.
